Severe Flooding Disrupts Real Estate Operations in Queensland

Flooding triggered by days of torrential rain has forced major disruptions across the Australian real estate sector, with numerous agency offices, property management sites, and property development premises reporting significant damage in Queensland. The floodwaters, which began inundating parts of Brisbane and the Gold Coast late Monday, have rendered several high-profile real estate offices temporarily inoperable, while ongoing evacuations have affected staff and halted operations at multiple property development sites.

RealtyOne Group, a leading agency, said its main Brisbane office was “severely impacted,” with water entering the ground-floor reception and damaging essential records. “Our immediate concern is for the safety of our staff and clients,” said CEO Julie Manning. “We are working to secure our premises and salvage critical documents.” Similar reports have come from property management firms such as UrbanNest Realty and GoldRiver Estates, which cited waterlogged offices, inaccessible property assets, and the suspension of routine inspections.

Development sites have also suffered, with ongoing construction and open houses cancelled or postponed. “With sites under water, it’s impossible to safely continue showings or work,” said Daniel Tran, site manager at Horizon Developments, which has several projects near the Brisbane River. “We are monitoring the situation and will resume as soon as conditions allow.”

The Real Estate Industry Association of Australia (REIA) estimated that more than 20% of affected agencies in the region have closed their doors temporarily, impacting hundreds of workers. “The full extent of the damage remains unclear as floodwaters are yet to recede,” said REIA spokesperson Mark Edwards. “We anticipate a lengthy recovery for many local real estate businesses.” The flooding is ongoing, with further rainfall forecast in the coming days.
